clue.text: Does view oddly cut off blossom?

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered places of the words Does view

parts.note: to lop is to cut off a branch

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether pruning a view will spoil the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes D, E, V, E from 'Does view'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that blossoms grows and opens out; both verbs describe unfolding into fuller form.

clue.text: Heroic exploit about start of victory is made up

indicators.note: about says the exploit word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a deed is a heroic act

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of victory

explanation.surface: A tale of valour leading to triumph turns out to be invented.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that is invented or contrived has been dreamt up, as in a cleverly concocted scheme.

clue.text: Proud to capture bad criminal

indicators.note: to capture says the proud word holds the other inside

parts.note: vain means proud or conceited
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: An arrogant officer is out to catch a dangerous lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, especially in a story or crime, is a rogue or crook: a noun synonym.

clue.text: Abandon holiday

definitions.meaning: to walk out on or desert someone
time off granted from work or the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for deserting and the noun for permitted time away from duty.

clue.text: 'Journalists outside Foreign Office turned up gold,' one declares

indicators.note: outside says the journalists' word goes around the office letters

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the UK foreign ministry
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A spokesperson announces that reporters near a government ministry found gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads letters bottom to top. The definition is cryptic: someone who professes is one who declares, though the word usually names an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who professes a belief openly states it, so one who declares; usually an academic title.

clue.text: Exceptional charm almost taking in agents

indicators.note: taking in says the shortened charm wraps around the agents
almost says the last letter of the charm word is dropped

parts.note: a spell is a magic charm
the CIA is the US agency of secret agents

explanation.surface: Someone remarkable nearly charms a group of spies into their circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' means the charm word loses its last letter before it opens up around the agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean out of the ordinary, unusual and better than normal: plain synonyms.

clue.text: Second drink for fun

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone has another glass just for the enjoyment of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for amusement is doing it for a laugh, as in 'it was good fun'.

clue.text: In wrapping of parcel I'm in a temper, getting stamp out

indicators.note: In wrapping of says the letters are wrapped inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone wrapping a parcel loses their temper and gets a postage stamp out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamp out' looks like part of the parcel scene, but it is the definition: to eradicate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp out something is to get rid of it entirely, to eradicate it.

clue.text: Ape? I'm worried to follow it

indicators.note: to follow says the word for worried comes after it

parts.note: ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: Someone frets about being told to copy a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape?' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning copy. 'Worried' gives ATE: something that is eating you worries you.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or copy them, from monkeys' supposed copying.

clue.text: Forgiving Russian leader neglecting latest new hospital department

indicators.note: neglecting latest says the final letter is dropped from the leader's name

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian revolution
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler overlooks the newest hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A merciful, tolerant person is ready to pardon, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Coal, no scuttles? After five it's probably covered in ash

indicators.note: After says the jumbled letters come after the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: scuttles suggests scurrying about, so the letters of coal and no are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone empties the coal scuttle after five o'clock, and the hearth is left full of ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scuttles' looks like the coal bucket from the surface, but here it is a verb telling you to jumble the coal word, giving OLCA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain that erupts is typically blanketed in ash from past eruptions, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Feeling nothing, bolt attached to one leg

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a pin is a bolt or peg
the Roman numeral I is one
on is the leg side in cricket, the side the batsman stands on

explanation.surface: A numb patient has a metal bolt fixed to their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: ON for 'leg' is cricket: the leg side, where the batsman's legs are, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling about something is a view or belief held about it, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Government fellows given time to provide formal account

parts.note: the state is the government
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Officials are given extra time to submit an official report.
explanation.definitionFit: An official written or spoken record of facts is a declaration of this kind.

clue.text: Cross I value highly

parts.note: to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: Someone who is annoyed insists that they think a lot of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb or a noun but is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being angry, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Welcoming knight, stops working and eats

indicators.note: Welcoming says the broken-down word takes the knight into its middle

parts.note: a machine that dies stops working
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An engine breaks down as it lets in a knight, while somebody has a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a meal, especially the main one of the day.

clue.text: Tiniest moan about large cricket match

indicators.note: about says the moan word goes round the large letter

parts.note: a sigh is a moan
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A grumble over a big international cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket match lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the very least in size or amount, as in the faintest idea.

clue.text: American city removing old religious symbol

indicators.note: removing says a letter is taken away from the city's name

parts.note: Sacramento is the capital city of California

explanation.surface: A US city is getting rid of an antique emblem of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites such as baptism and the Eucharist are outward signs of grace, so a symbolic religious rite.

clue.text: Curse most wicked clients

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters are twisted and bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper swears at the nastiest of the people they serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers or clients are the people who buy from a business, a synonym.

clue.text: Playing this, is ball I'd planned to pot right?

indicators.note: to pot is to sink a ball in a pocket, so the right letter goes inside
planned says the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A player at the table asks whether the ball they meant to sink is on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' turns IS BALL I'D into BILLIADS, and 'to pot' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The question describes a cue game played on a cloth table where balls are sunk in pockets.

clue.text: Liberal seen in club with six-footer, unashamed

indicators.note: seen in says the Liberal letter appears inside the club word

parts.note: a bat is a club
an ant is an insect with six feet

explanation.surface: A politician walks into a club with a very tall companion, quite shamelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect, which has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant, shameless behaviour is done openly without embarrassment, a synonym.

clue.text: Loss of water, perhaps, could come from e.g. a lake

indicators.note: could come from says the letters are reworked to produce the result

explanation.surface: Water lost from a pond or lake is a natural observation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could come from' tells you to rearrange E.G. A LAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Water escaping through a hole is one example of a fluid seeping out, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Moved slowly and didn't middle the ball

definitions.meaning: to edge forward is to move slowly and carefully
in cricket a batsman who fails to hit the ball with the middle of the bat catches it off the bat's thin side

explanation.surface: A batsman creeps forward and then mistimes the delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle' is cricket jargon for hitting the ball cleanly with the centre of the bat; the opposite is getting a thin touch off the bat's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Inching forward and nicking a ball off the bat's side share one verb in cricket and in ordinary English.

clue.text: See good politicians getting trapped by falsehood

indicators.note: getting trapped by says the politicians sit inside the falsehood

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Decent politicians end up caught out by a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something briefly is to see it, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Flower with blight — that's most serious

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Dee is a British river
a pest is a blight or plague

explanation.surface: A gardener whose bloom has a disease calls it the gravest case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword joke for a river, something that flows; the Dee runs through Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep trouble or thoughts are serious, so the superlative means the most grave or profound.

clue.text: A waterway initially remains flooded

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word waterway

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A canal, at first, stays waterlogged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swamped or covered with water is drenched, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Inflammation resulting from cold? Doctor best for it

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient with a chill-related swelling is told the doctor knows the best treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a medic in this medical scene but is the instruction to rearrange BEST FOR IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Freezing injures skin and flesh, leaving them red and swollen, so an injury caused by cold.

clue.text: Pressure in support of church

parts.note: being for something is supporting it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Lobbying on behalf of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Force and pressure both mean a push or compulsion, as in to pressure someone.

clue.text: Slice over small bunkers

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the word is turned upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a part is a slice or portion

explanation.surface: A golfer slices the ball over small sand hazards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slice' looks like a golf shot here but means a portion; bunkers are sand hazards on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf bunkers are hazards that catch balls, so they are snares on the course.

clue.text: Lay a rug, with regret, the wrong way round

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

indicators.note: the wrong way round says the word for regret is written backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone puts a rug down, then regrets having laid it facing the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning non-professional, as in lay preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay person is not a professional or expert, which is what a non-professional enthusiast is.

clue.text: Former lover with sufficient warning

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means enough or sufficient

explanation.surface: A former partner gave plenty of notice of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishment that serves as a warning to others is meant to deter, as in 'make one of them'.

clue.text: A conclusion to act is seen in there

definitions.text: A conclusion to act is seen in there

indicators.note: is seen in says the letters sit inside the word there
conclusion to picks out the final letter of the word act

explanation.surface: The curtain falls on an act in a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is where a play's acts are performed and reach their end, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Defendant: 'PC set us up!'

indicators.note: set up means arranged, so the letters of PC set us are put together anew

explanation.surface: The accused complains in the dock that a police officer framed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set us up' sounds like a framing; 'up' asks for PCSETUS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The person accused of a crime is one under suspicion, the accused party in court.
